paper_title: TRUTH DECAY Quantifying Multi-Turn Sycophancy in Language Models
caption: Average Change Per Followup, Claude MMLU-Pro. When a LLM originally answers incorrectly, it experiences up to 40% higher change percentages than when it has an initially correct answer.

annotations.annotation: The line plot illustrates the average change percentage of answers, categorized by their initial accuracy, as a function of the turn number. The x-axis is labeled "Turn Number", utilizing a linear scale ranging from 1 to 7 with integer intervals of 1. The y-axis is labeled "Average Change Percentage (%)" and also uses a linear scale, ranging from 10 to 50 with tick label intervals set at increments of 10. The first line, representing "Initial Correct Answer", is red with a solid line style and circular markers. It starts at approximately 2% on the y-axis at turn 1, increasing steadily to around 11% by turn 3, and then remains unchanged through turn 7. The second line, representing "Initial Incorrect Answer", is yellow, also with a solid line and circular markers. This line begins at approximately 17% at turn 1, rises steadily to about 25% by turn 3, then sharply increases to 49% at turn 4 and maintains this value through turn 7. A legend is given top left.
